content: The study compares the use of inhaled corticosteroids (ICS), specifically Budesonide and Ciclesonide, against standard of care (SOC) in the treatment of COVID-19. The findings are presented in a series of forest plots, each addressing specific outcomes in different patient populations. Below are the detailed descriptions of the outcomes analyzed: 1. Risk of Bias Summary: The authors evaluated the risk of bias for each included study, providing a summary of their judgments for each bias-related item. 2. Budesonide vs. Standard Care for Early COVID-19: Clinical Recovery Time (Days): A forest plot compares the time to clinical recovery between patients treated with Budesonide and those receiving standard care. Urgent Hospital Visits: Another forest plot examines the frequency of urgent hospital visits in the Budesonide group versus the standard care group. 3. Budesonide vs. Standard Care for High-Risk Patients: Mortality: A forest plot evaluates the impact of Budesonide on mortality rates in high-risk patients compared to standard care. Clinical Recovery Time (Days): The time to clinical recovery is compared between the two groups. Alleviation of All Symptoms: The analysis investigates the resolution of all symptoms in patients treated with Budesonide versus standard care. Intensive Care Unit (ICU) Admission: The likelihood of ICU admission is compared between the two groups. Mechanical Ventilation: The need for mechanical ventilation is analyzed in patients receiving Budesonide versus standard care. 4. Ciclesonide vs. Standard Care for Mild to Moderate COVID-19: Mortality at 28–30 Days: A forest plot assesses the mortality rate within 28 to 30 days in patients treated with Ciclesonide compared to standard care. Clinical Improvement at 14 Days: The rate of clinical improvement at 14 days is compared between the two groups. Hospitalization at 14 Days: The frequency of hospitalization within 14 days is analyzed for patients receiving Ciclesonide versus standard care. Duration of Hospitalization (Days): The length of hospital stay is compared between the two groups. Clinical Improvement at 7 Days: The rate of clinical improvement at 7 days is evaluated for patients treated with Ciclesonide versus standard care. Each of these outcomes is visualized using forest plots, which provide a graphical representation of the comparative effectiveness of inhaled corticosteroids versus standard care in various patient populations and clinical scenarios. The analyses were conducted using Review Manager (RevMan) software, version 5.4.1.
